name: Close the books monthly
summary: Each month the finance team closes the ledger and produces results by service line and district for management, and at quarter-end the package for the public financial statements. Billing specialists and district administrators work out which completed jobs have no signed field ticket yet so that revenue can be accrued, accounts payable accrues goods received but not invoiced, inventory counts are posted, and about eight accountants prepare accruals, capitalise equipment upgrades, reconcile balance sheet accounts and post journals. A financial analyst explains variances with district managers, the controller reviews and the CFO signs off the management report. Unsigned field tickets, late supplier invoices for sand, trucking and parts, and spreadsheet reconciliations are what make the close slow and the accruals uncertain.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people, roughly 880 of them field staff on rotation or on call at nine district bases, with a Calgary head office for finance, HR, HSE and engineering.
baseline.notes: ERP general ledger with sub-ledgers for billing, payables, inventory and fixed assets; close checklist and reconciliations in Excel on a shared drive; journal approval by signature or email; no reconciliation or close management software.

trigger: The calendar month ends; the close calendar starts on the first working day of the next month.
end_state: The period is locked in the ERP, balance sheet accounts are reconciled and reviewed, and the controller and CFO have issued the monthly management report by service line (at quarter-end also the package for quarterly reporting).

volume.seasonality: One close a month. Quarter-end closes (March, June, September, December) carry extra work: tax provision, impairment indicators, covenant calculations and the auditor's review; year-end is the heaviest. Revenue accruals are hardest in busy winter months with the most unsigned tickets.

evidence.note: One close a month by definition.

surge.cause: Quarter-end and year-end close for public reporting and the external auditor

evidence.note: Listed issuers file interim statements each quarter; the extra effort per quarter-end close (30-100% more accountant hours) is the author's estimate.
Ten accountants; about eight take part in each close for roughly the first six working days, plus reconciliations through the month.

steps.name: Send close calendar and cut-off reminders
steps.description: The controller sends the close calendar with due dates by day, reminds districts to release field tickets and goods receipts and confirms the date the sub-ledgers will be closed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: List completed jobs without invoices
steps.description: Billing specialists run the job list from the field ticket system and ERP, mark every job completed in the month that has not been invoiced, and record why: ticket unsigned on the customer's portal, disputed, or not yet priced.

error.defect_description: A completed job is missed or listed twice

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Confirm open ticket status with the bases
steps.description: District administrators check each open ticket on the list, add the expected amount from the price book and job notes, and chase customer field supervisors for signatures that would let the job be invoiced before the cut-off.

error.defect_description: Estimated amount for an unsigned ticket differs from what the customer later approves

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Accrue goods received not invoiced
steps.description: AP clerks run the received-not-invoiced report, add sand, trucking, fuel and rental charges known from load tickets and supplier statements but not yet invoiced, and send the accrual list to accounting.

error.defect_description: A large haul or sand invoice is not accrued

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Post inventory counts and adjustments
steps.description: The inventory controller posts month-end counts of sand, chemicals, cement and parts from the bases and plants, investigates large differences with the warehouse and books the adjustments.

error.defect_description: A count keyed in the wrong unit of measure

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Close sub-ledgers
steps.description: The ERP closes billing, payables, inventory and fixed asset sub-ledgers for the month, runs depreciation and posts the sub-ledger totals to the general ledger.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Prepare revenue and cost accruals
steps.description: Accountants turn the unbilled jobs and cost accrual lists into journal entries by service line and district, accrue payroll for days worked but not paid and bonuses, and reverse last month's accruals.

error.defect_description: Revenue accrued at the wrong price or for a job later billed in the month

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Capitalise upgrades and update fixed assets
steps.description: An accountant moves completed equipment upgrade and rebuild costs from capital work in progress to fixed assets, checks capital versus repair coding on large work orders and books disposals.

error.defect_description: Repair cost capitalised or capital cost expensed

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Reconcile balance sheet accounts
steps.description: Accountants reconcile cash, receivables, unbilled revenue, inventory, prepaid, fixed asset, payroll clearing, accrued liabilities and tax accounts in Excel templates, each to sub-ledger reports, bank statements or schedules, and explain reconciling items.

error.defect_description: A reconciling item carried forward without being cleared

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Post journals with approval
steps.description: Each journal with its support is approved by an accountant other than the preparer or by the controller above the threshold, then posted to the ledger.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: journal entries approved by someone other than the preparer (NI 52-109 certification)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review reconciliations
steps.description: The controller reviews the key reconciliations for cash, unbilled revenue, inventory, accruals and payroll clearing, signs them off or sends back items that are unexplained or aged.

control.basis: Documented review of balance sheet reconciliations relied on by the external auditor

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Build flux analysis by service line
steps.description: A financial analyst pulls the trial balance into the reporting workbook, compares revenue, margin and costs by service line and district with last month, budget and job counts, and lists every variance above the threshold.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Get variance explanations from districts
steps.description: The analyst emails or calls district managers about unusual costs, margins and job counts, and they explain from what they know of the month: repairs, standby, a lost customer or a price change.

next.condition: error found that needs a journal

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Book correcting entries
steps.description: An accountant books the correcting or missed accrual found in the variance review, attaches the district manager's explanation as support and re-runs the trial balance for the analyst.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Controller reviews preliminary results
steps.description: The controller reads the results by service line with the variance explanations, challenges accruals and estimates such as unsigned tickets and bonuses, and either accepts the numbers or asks for top-side adjustments.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Lock the period
steps.description: An accountant runs the last checks, closes the period in the ERP so no further postings can be made and saves the trial balance.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Prepare management report
steps.description: The financial analyst updates the monthly report with revenue, adjusted EBITDA and margin by service line, jobs, revenue per job, fleet utilisation, headcount and capital spending, with comments on the month.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: CFO reviews and releases report
steps.description: The CFO reads the report, asks for clarifications on large variances and releases it to the executive team and service line directors.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Distribute results
steps.description: The analyst sends the report and service line packs to executives, service line directors and district managers, and loads actuals into the forecast model.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Prepare quarter-end schedules
steps.description: At quarter-end accountants add the tax provision, impairment indicator review, provisions, lease and share-based compensation schedules and the covenant calculation that the quarterly statements and lenders need.

error.defect_description: A schedule does not tie to the trial balance

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Controller signs off quarter-end package
steps.description: The controller ties the schedules to the trial balance, reviews the judgements and hands the package to the reporting team and the external auditor's review.

control.basis: NI 52-109 CEO and CFO certification of interim filings; interim statements filed within 45 days of quarter-end (NI 51-102)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Unsigned field tickets at cut-off
exceptions.description: Every month some completed jobs have no customer-approved ticket, so revenue is accrued at estimated amounts and corrected when invoiced.

exceptions.name: Controller changes an accrual
exceptions.description: The controller's review changes an estimate and the accruals, reconciliations and analysis are redone.

exceptions.name: Variance reveals a missed entry
exceptions.description: A district manager's explanation shows a missed accrual or miscoding and a correcting entry is booked.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end
exceptions.description: Quarter-end months add tax, impairment, covenant and disclosure schedules for the quarterly statements.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from running the trial balance to completed consolidated statements
benchmarks.population: About 2,300 organisations in APQC's Open Standards Benchmarking (published 2018); median 6.4, bottom quartile 10 or more days

evidence.note: APQC median and bottom-quartile values (src5). The p90 is set at the bottom-quartile threshold, which understates the true 90th percentile.

pain_points.description: Revenue for jobs without signed tickets must be estimated job by job from the field and corrected later.

evidence.note: Organisation file description of unsigned field tickets; frequency is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Supplier invoices for sand, trucking and parts arrive weeks after the work, so large cost accruals depend on load tickets and supplier statements.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Reconciliations and the flux analysis are built by hand in Excel each month and most of the work is squeezed into the first week.

evidence.note: APQC names data quality and month-end workload concentration as the main barriers to a faster close (src5).

pain_points.description: Explanations wait for district managers who are busy with operations.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of how Canadian oilfield service companies ran this work in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Metric of the Month: Cycle Time for Monthly Close
sources.supports: APQC Open Standards Benchmarking, about 2,300 organisations: cycle time from running the trial balance to consolidated statements is 4.8 days or less for the top quartile, 6.4 days at the median and 10 or more days for the bottom quartile; barriers are mostly data quality, non-standard charts of accounts and workload concentrated at month-end.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).
The case runs from the first working day after month-end to the released management report (or quarter-end package); preparatory work during the month is excluded.
Triggered_by shares are the author's split of the ledger postings each feeding process contributes; the close starts on the calendar, not on any one posting.

Billing specialists, district administrators, AP clerks, the inventory controller, district managers and the CFO take part although the process map lists only accountants, the controller and financial analysts.
Field tickets from fo-dist-field-ticket-preparation are added as an input because unsigned tickets drive the revenue accrual.

The APQC benchmark is cross-industry and measures trial balance to consolidated statements; the simulated cycle also includes the CFO's release, so it can run longer than the benchmark (simulated median about 9 days against 6.4).

Stated FTE (about 7.3) is more than twice the hands-on time of one close because accountants and analysts also reconcile accounts, review costs and answer audit requests during the rest of the month, which is not modelled as close steps.
